name: Delaware

events.title: Ratified the Constitution
events.text: Delaware ratified the Constitution on December 7, 1787, the 1st state to do so. The Constitution gave it 1 seat in the House until the first census.

events.title: 1790 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1790 census, Delaware kept 1 seat in the House. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

events.title: 1800 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1800 census, Delaware kept 1 seat in the House. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

events.title: 1810 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1810 census, Delaware's House delegation grew from 1 to 2 seats.

events.title: Statewide (general ticket) elections
events.text: In the 13th through 17th Congresses (1813–1823), Delaware elected all of its representatives statewide on a general ticket instead of by district.

events.title: 1820 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1820 census, Delaware's House delegation shrank from 2 to 1 seat. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

compactnessNote: Polsby-Popper compactness (4π × area ÷ perimeter²) measured on the projected district shapes. It describes shape only: coastlines, rivers and county lines lower it too, so a low score is not evidence of intent. "Irregular" marks the least compact 5% of district shapes in each census era nationally.
